final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is mainly a narrower interpretation of the same facts: aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incident occurred, the refund workflow segment remains below target, that segment remains exposed in rollout, and no completed approved risk acceptance covers that exposure. That narrowing is useful, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. On the policy text available here, rollout controls, rollback, monitoring, and small-percentage rollout do not cure the issue when the affected use case remains exposed unless exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance exists. The Actor's caveated position is therefore more defensible than a clean-compliance claim, but it still falls short of establishing compliant or compliant_with_caveats from admissible evidence alone. The unresolved issue is not merely a disclosure detail; it is an unmet policy condition for an exposed materially weak segment.
